newsitem.title: RUSSIA: CIS GDP fell six pct in 1996 after 3.9 pct 95 fall.
newsitem.headline: CIS GDP fell six pct in 1996 after 3.9 pct 95 fall.

text.p: The economy of the Commonwealth of Independent States continued to shrink overall in 1996, although some individual members are seeing output increase from a low base, the CIS Interstate Statistics Committee said.
CIS gross domestic product (GDP) fell six percent in 1996 after falling 3.9 percent in 1995, the committee said in a bulletin.
The economy is now only 59 percent of its size in 1991, when the former Soviet Union broke up, and has returned to levels last seen in 1977.
It is 53 percent of its level in 1989 when the economy peaked before going into decline in the last years of the Soviet Union.
The CIS comprises all the former republics of the Soviet Union except the Baltic states of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia.

The overall figures for the CIS were dragged down by its biggest member, Russia, whose economy at 61 percent of 1991 levels is now the size last seen in 1979. The economy of another big CIS member, Ukraine, also shrank sharply in 1996.
But Armenia, whose economy started to recover in 1994, notched up another year of growth, though its economy is only at 1975 levels.
Two other Transcaucasian states, Georgia and Azerbaijan, also grew last year, but their economies are still only at 1963 levels.
